findings.title: Resolve ESP32Sim’s license before treating it as a foundation
findings.strength: Pinning the exact source snapshot is excellent provenance hygiene.
findings.evidence: No repository-root license file was found in the bundled ESP32Sim root `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim`. The public GitHub repository also reports no declared license as of the review date.
findings.impact: Without an explicit grant, copying, modifying, distributing, or shipping the upstream code can be legally blocked even when the repository is public. Component-level licenses do not automatically license the repository as a whole.
findings.change: Obtain an explicit license from the author or a signed contribution/license agreement; add a root LICENSE, NOTICE, source provenance record, and a third-party inventory before any product branch imports or modifies the code.
findings.acceptance: Legal/owner approval is recorded; the exact licensed commit is named; CI verifies required license/notice files; release artifacts carry the required notices.

findings.title: Turn the pinned snapshot into a reproducible upstream provenance record
findings.strength: The archive and fixtures use exact hashes, which is the right foundation.
findings.evidence: Archive SHA-256 is `32dbbd6890be1787bcbe22fbb7d0f57003ec4d69d4013fbc6adad67de0c05db1`; local git metadata is recorded for both roots in the review evidence. `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/MANIFEST.md:20`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/MANIFEST.md:81`
findings.impact: A source copy without an origin URL, commit, patch stack, license state, and update policy becomes difficult to audit or refresh safely.
findings.change: Create `third_party/esp32sim/PROVENANCE.md` with upstream URL, exact commit, retrieval date, archive hash, local patch series, license, and approved update procedure.
findings.acceptance: A clean script can fetch the approved commit, verify its hash, apply the patch series, and reproduce the vendored tree byte-for-byte.

findings.title: Inventory redistribution rights for ROMs, firmware blobs, fonts, audio, and calibration fixtures
findings.strength: The project preserves high-value real-world fixtures rather than relying only on synthetic examples.
findings.evidence: The supplied archive contains binary fixtures and calibration material; the largest-file hash inventory is in the companion evidence. License/notice files found: 12. `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:87`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:93`
findings.impact: A technically reproducible test corpus can still be non-redistributable. Firmware built from third-party SDKs, mask ROM images, media, and generated assets may each have different rights.
findings.change: Add an asset manifest with source, author, license/permission, whether redistribution is allowed, whether the asset may be public, and the build recipe. Keep restricted fixtures in a separately controlled store.
findings.acceptance: Every non-source artifact has an owner, digest, origin, rights field, retention rule, and reproducible generation command.

findings.title: Adopt ESP32Sim as a controlled fork, not as a stable external API
findings.strength: The upstream author documents decisions and validates against hardware unusually well for an early emulator.
findings.evidence: Public repository metadata shows the project was created on 2026-08-25 and the reviewed public head was `2114ffc92039b4605264d2cfb4ee5543acbf98c1` on 2026-08-30; it had no tagged compatibility contract or declared license at review time.
findings.impact: Rapid, single-maintainer development is productive, but internal types and behavior can change faster than Puck can safely absorb.
findings.change: Mirror/fork the approved commit, protect the fork, keep Puck-facing APIs in a narrow adapter crate/package, and upstream changes selectively after conformance review.
findings.acceptance: Puck builds against one documented adapter version; upstream syncs are isolated PRs with full differential and security test results.

findings.title: Pin CI actions and downloaded toolchain artifacts by immutable digest
findings.strength: The repository already treats firmware and fixture hashes as important evidence.
findings.evidence: Workflow files inspected: puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/.github/workflows/pages.yml, puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/.github/workflows/verify-bundles.yml. Action references and network fetches should be checked against immutable SHAs and file digests. `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/.github/workflows/pages.yml:39`
findings.impact: Tags, branches, and unverified downloads can change after review, turning CI into a supply-chain execution path.
findings.change: Pin every GitHub Action to a full commit SHA, use minimal permissions, verify downloaded ROM/toolchain/archive SHA-256 values, and record approved update automation.
findings.acceptance: A policy test rejects mutable `uses:` refs and network downloads without a verified digest.

findings.title: Make generated fixtures visibly generated and reviewable
findings.strength: Golden displays, audio, and traces provide strong regression sensitivity.
findings.evidence: The archive includes built fixtures with hashes; regression references appear in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:38`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:53`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:149`
findings.impact: When a fixture can be replaced by the same change that alters behavior, the test can silently ratify a defect.
findings.change: Store generator version, exact inputs, command, expected semantic summary, and reviewer checklist next to every fixture. Split behavior changes and golden updates into distinct commits where practical.
findings.acceptance: CI regenerates a sample set and compares hashes; fixture-update PRs show semantic diffs and require a second reviewer.

findings.title: Preserve the archive’s safe extraction and integrity properties
findings.strength: The reviewed archive can be hashed and inventoried as a single immutable handoff.
findings.evidence: Archive scan found 0 unsafe path entries and recorded 1783 files.
findings.impact: Future export tooling could accidentally admit absolute paths, `..` traversal, symlinks, or mutable external references.
findings.change: Keep safe-extraction checks in export/import tooling and generate a signed manifest of paths, sizes, modes, and hashes.
findings.acceptance: A hostile ZIP corpus proves traversal, symlink, duplicate-path, case-folding, and oversized-entry rejection.

findings.title: Add release-time secret scanning for both source and binaries
findings.strength: The upstream history shows awareness of embedded-secret risks, and the supplied project separates fixtures from core source.
findings.evidence: Static source scan recorded 0 potential secret-shaped strings for manual triage; binary fixtures also need `strings`/entropy scanning before publication.
findings.impact: Credentials can survive in firmware images, source maps, test logs, browser bundles, or old fixtures even when source files are clean.
findings.change: Run allowlisted secret scanners over text, git history, generated bundles, firmware strings, and release archives; redact logs and rotate any confirmed credential.
findings.acceptance: A release candidate fails closed on unapproved hits, with explicit fixture allowlists tied to hashes.

findings.title: Define an agent-safe change protocol
findings.strength: The project’s roadmap and evidence documents give agents useful context.
findings.evidence: `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:1`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:11`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:1`
findings.impact: Multiple autonomous agents can independently “fix” the same boundary, update goldens, or widen APIs without sharing the same assumptions.
findings.change: Require a short ADR/change brief for architecture, guest-host ABI, timing, fixture, or upstream-sync changes. Assign file ownership and one integration agent per milestone.
findings.acceptance: Every qualifying PR names the invariant changed, evidence added, rollback path, and affected compatibility matrix.

findings.title: Add an explicit dependency and toolchain update policy
findings.strength: The present dependency surface is small, which makes disciplined updates practical.
findings.evidence: Puck declares 0 runtime and 5 development dependencies; ESP32Sim’s Cargo workspace is similarly compact.
findings.impact: Unscheduled upgrades can break determinism, browser output, transpilation, or generated fixture hashes; indefinite pinning can accumulate security debt.
findings.change: Pin exact toolchain versions, use scheduled update PRs, require changelog review, and rerun the full conformance matrix before merging.
findings.acceptance: Lockfiles, runtime versions, and build images are immutable in release branches; automated updates are isolated and reversible.

findings.title: Use one mandatory guest-output validator in live, headless, replay, and verification paths
findings.strength: The live canvas path already validates important framebuffer/push results—a strong start.
findings.evidence: Framebuffer/canvas and headless/replay code are separate call paths: `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/abiGuard.ts:95`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/abiGuard.ts:124`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/panel.ts:20`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/panel.ts:49`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/panel.ts:55`
findings.impact: A malformed firmware/module can bypass the live-path checks and crash, allocate excessively, or corrupt the headless regression path—the very path intended to be trusted proof.
findings.change: Move pointer/range/dimension/stride/count validation into a pure shared boundary module. All consumers must receive validated value objects, never raw guest pointers.
findings.acceptance: The same hostile module corpus is run against every host mode and produces the same typed failure without process crash, hang, allocation spike, or partial artifact.

findings.title: Harden every WASI-lite import as an untrusted ABI
findings.strength: A deliberately small WASI surface is much safer than importing a general host runtime.
findings.evidence: WASI-related imports, including `fd_write`, are present at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/README.md:25`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/src/wasi_support.cpp:7`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/src/wasi_support.cpp:14`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/abi.md:244`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/wasm.ts:216`
findings.impact: Guest-provided iovec pointers, counts, lengths, clocks, and buffers can overflow arithmetic, cross memory bounds, trigger very large copies, or flood logs unless checked before dereference.
findings.change: Implement checked `u64` arithmetic, memory-range validation after every memory refresh, caps on iovec count and total bytes, bounded UTF-8 decoding, deterministic clock/random behavior, and explicit errno returns.
findings.acceptance: Property tests and hostile modules cover wraparound, out-of-bounds, zero-length edge cases, memory growth, huge counts, invalid UTF-8, closed descriptors, and log quotas.

findings.title: Put hard resource ceilings on guest-directed work
findings.strength: The architecture is already amenable to deterministic budgeting.
findings.evidence: Guest output and memory-related code appears in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/wasm-plan.md:80`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/timing_verify.ts:37`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/abiGuard.ts:63`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/abiGuard.ts:143`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/panel.ts:116`
findings.impact: Valid-but-extreme dimensions, row counts, log sizes, event queues, sample counts, and memory pages can exhaust the browser, CI runner, or verifier without an out-of-bounds bug.
findings.change: Define per-run limits for Wasm pages, instruction/cycle budget, wall time, frames, pixels, audio samples, output bytes, queue depth, recursion/nesting, and artifact size. Reject before allocation.
findings.acceptance: Boundary tests hit every limit and one-past-limit case; telemetry records which quota ended a run.

findings.title: Refresh typed-array views after WebAssembly memory growth
findings.strength: Using direct typed-array views is efficient and appropriate when lifecycle is explicit.
findings.evidence: Wasm memory construction/access points are referenced at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/wasm-plan.md:80`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/timing_verify.ts:37`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/abiGuard.ts:63`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/abiGuard.ts:143`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/panel.ts:116`
findings.impact: A `memory.grow` detaches or replaces the underlying buffer; cached views can become stale and validators can inspect a different buffer from the consumer.
findings.change: Centralize memory access behind a view provider keyed by `memory.buffer`; reacquire views before each boundary operation and after guest calls that may grow memory.
findings.acceptance: A hostile fixture grows memory between pointer production and host read; all modes either read the new valid range or reject deterministically.

findings.title: Make cancellation and timeouts preemptive rather than cooperative
findings.strength: Headless execution already provides a natural place to enforce deterministic budgets.
findings.evidence: `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:38`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:53`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:149`
findings.impact: A guest stuck in an infinite loop, interrupt storm, or path that never yields can block the worker or CI process before host-side checks run.
findings.change: Run untrusted execution in a disposable Worker/process with instruction or cycle slicing, wall-clock watchdog, memory cap, and forced termination. Keep artifact writing outside that process.
findings.acceptance: An infinite-loop specimen terminates within the deadline, releases memory, and leaves no partial “passed” result.

findings.title: Normalize and confine every host filesystem path
findings.strength: Separating fixtures and generated outputs is a good basis for a confined workspace.
findings.evidence: Replay/build/fixture references occur in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:38`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:53`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:149`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:157`
findings.impact: Manifest names, test IDs, module names, or guest-supplied strings can become traversal paths, overwrite fixtures, or escape an output directory.
findings.change: Treat all external names as identifiers, not paths. Generate internal filenames, resolve beneath a dedicated root, reject separators/control characters/case collisions, and write atomically with no-follow semantics.
findings.acceptance: Traversal, absolute-path, symlink, device-name, Unicode-normalization, and case-folding tests cannot escape the sandbox.

findings.title: Default ESP32Sim networking to no egress for untrusted firmware
findings.strength: ESP32Sim’s user-mode network is a valuable integration capability and its browser build naturally has no raw host sockets.
findings.evidence: Network/socket code appears at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:139`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:156`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:31`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/README.md:12`
findings.impact: A native NAT bridge lets arbitrary guest firmware probe localhost, private networks, developer services, cloud metadata endpoints, or exfiltrate data through DNS/HTTP. This is SSRF from a guest VM.
findings.change: Use `net=none` by default in Puck. Put optional egress behind explicit user consent and a policy layer that blocks loopback, link-local, RFC1918/ULA, multicast, metadata ranges, rebinding, and excessive flows; support destination allowlists.
findings.acceptance: Hostile firmware cannot reach protected address classes; DNS answers are revalidated at connect time; rate and byte limits are enforced.

findings.title: Constrain local WebSocket/UI control surfaces
findings.strength: A live board UI is an excellent observability tool.
findings.evidence: WebSocket/server references appear at Repository-wide inspection of the supplied snapshot.
findings.impact: A listener bound beyond loopback, missing Origin checks, or unauthenticated control messages can let another site or LAN peer operate the emulator, load firmware, or read output.
findings.change: Bind loopback by default, use a random capability token, validate Origin/Host, cap message sizes and rates, and require an explicit flag for remote binding with TLS/authentication.
findings.acceptance: Cross-site WebSocket attempts, oversized frames, invalid message types, and LAN connections are rejected by default.

findings.title: Validate every Worker/WebSocket event against a versioned schema
findings.strength: The project already uses explicit message types, which is a good protocol foundation.
findings.evidence: WebSocket/event message handling appears at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:243`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:53`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:187`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/speed-plan.md:132`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/examples/waveshare-cam/README.md:6`
findings.impact: Unchecked message shapes, numeric coercions, duplicate fields, large arrays, or unknown versions can produce inconsistent behavior across browser, native, and test paths.
findings.change: Define a closed discriminated schema with strict numeric bounds, maximum payload sizes, protocol version, and unknown-field policy. Validate before dispatch.
findings.acceptance: A protocol corpus covers missing, extra, duplicate, malformed, very large, old-version, and future-version messages in all transports.

findings.title: Make time, randomness, and external input explicit deterministic services
findings.strength: Deterministic fixtures and exact output hashes show the project values reproducibility.
findings.evidence: WASI clock/random and replay references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:14`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:90`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:178`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:194`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:195`
findings.impact: Reading host time, entropy, scheduling, DNS, or network responses directly makes failures irreproducible and can cause browser/headless divergence.
findings.change: Inject clock, RNG seed, input event stream, and network transcript through a run context. Record them in the result manifest and separate “deterministic replay” from “live integration” modes.
findings.acceptance: Repeated runs with the same manifest are byte-identical; live-mode nondeterminism is labeled and excluded from exact golden assertions.

findings.title: Use a typed, fail-closed error model at the guest boundary
findings.strength: The current validators demonstrate the right instinct to reject malformed results.
findings.evidence: Error/validation sites are adjacent to `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/README.md:25`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/src/wasi_support.cpp:7`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/src/wasi_support.cpp:14`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/abi.md:244`
findings.impact: Generic exceptions, panics, or “best effort” continuation can convert a guest fault into partial output that looks valid or hide which invariant failed.
findings.change: Return structured errors with phase, code, guest address/range (redacted as needed), quota, and recoverability. On integrity faults, stop the run and discard uncommitted artifacts.
findings.acceptance: Every hostile fixture maps to one stable error code; no invalid run is reported as passed or produces a blessed golden.

findings.title: Commit output atomically only after full validation
findings.strength: The project’s artifact orientation makes transactional output practical.
findings.evidence: `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:65`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:74`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:75`
findings.impact: Writing rows, frames, logs, or audio incrementally before validation can leave partial artifacts after a late fault; CI may compare or publish them.
findings.change: Stage output in bounded temporary storage, validate final metadata and hash, then atomically rename/commit. Mark incomplete runs separately.
findings.acceptance: Killing a run at every write boundary never replaces the previous known-good artifact and never yields a pass marker.

findings.title: Run regression verification in a disposable isolation boundary
findings.strength: Headless replay is the right automation interface.
findings.evidence: `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:38`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:53`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:149`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:157`
findings.impact: A verifier sharing a process with untrusted Wasm, parsers, or image/audio encoders can be crashed or poisoned, invalidating the proof layer.
findings.change: Split execution from adjudication: a sandboxed worker emits a capped, schema-validated result bundle; a smaller trusted verifier checks hashes and semantics in a separate process.
findings.acceptance: Crashes, timeouts, and malformed result bundles become failed runs while the verifier and subsequent jobs remain healthy.

findings.title: Cap package/archive expansion before allocation
findings.strength: Content-addressed artifacts are a strong base for safe caching.
findings.evidence: `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:87`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:93`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:126`
findings.impact: A small compressed input or manifest can expand into an oversized module, image, trace, or nested archive and exhaust memory or disk.
findings.change: Apply limits to compressed size, uncompressed total, entry count, per-entry size, nesting, compression ratio, and duplicate paths before extraction; stream hashes.
findings.acceptance: ZIP-bomb, duplicate-name, nested, sparse, and huge-metadata corpora are rejected without exceeding resource budgets.

findings.title: Canonicalize registry and manifest identifiers once
findings.strength: The registry/pack model creates a natural validation choke point.
findings.evidence: Hash/integrity and registry-oriented evidence appears in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:87`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:93`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:126`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:115`
findings.impact: Unicode confusables, normalization differences, path-like names, semver ambiguity, and case-folding can create duplicate identities or cache/signature mismatches.
findings.change: Define ASCII or normalized identifier grammar, canonical semver, sorted canonical serialization, duplicate-key rejection, and one content digest computed over canonical bytes.
findings.acceptance: Cross-runtime canonicalization vectors produce identical bytes/digests; ambiguous identifiers and duplicate JSON keys are rejected.

findings.title: Ship browser isolation headers and a restrictive CSP
findings.strength: Running substantial emulation in a Worker is already a useful containment layer.
findings.evidence: Browser and WebAssembly code appears at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:224`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:225`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/server.ts:183`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/server.ts:185`
findings.impact: Without a strong CSP and cross-origin isolation policy, an unrelated script compromise can control firmware inputs/outputs; future shared memory features may be enabled inconsistently.
findings.change: Use no inline script where feasible, hashed/static assets, `object-src none`, narrow `connect-src`, COOP/COEP where required, and explicit worker sources. Avoid third-party runtime scripts.
findings.acceptance: Automated browser tests assert response headers and show no CSP violations in supported deployment modes.

findings.title: Treat guest logs and labels as untrusted display data
findings.strength: Exposing serial/log output is essential for emulator usability.
findings.evidence: `fd_write` and web UI output paths appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/README.md:25`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/src/wasi_support.cpp:7`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/puck/src/wasi_support.cpp:14`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/abi.md:244`
findings.impact: ANSI control sequences, terminal hyperlinks, bidi controls, HTML injection, huge lines, and high-rate output can spoof diagnostics or degrade the UI.
findings.change: Render as text, strip or visibly encode dangerous controls, cap line length/rate/total bytes, and preserve raw bytes only in a quarantined downloadable artifact.
findings.acceptance: A log-fuzz corpus cannot inject DOM, hide prior text, create links, or exceed quotas.

findings.title: Version and quota persistent browser state
findings.strength: Persisted packs and fixtures can make iteration fast and offline-friendly.
findings.evidence: Browser/package-related code appears at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:224`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:225`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/server.ts:183`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/server.ts:185`
findings.impact: Unbounded IndexedDB/cache state, schema drift, or partially written entries can strand users or cause old code to load incompatible modules.
findings.change: Use content-addressed entries, per-origin quotas, schema version/migrations, atomic writes, LRU cleanup, and a safe reset path.
findings.acceptance: Upgrade/downgrade/corruption tests recover without loading unverified content or losing unrelated user data.

findings.title: Define interrupt-storm and event-queue backpressure behavior
findings.strength: The emulator roadmap recognizes timing and peripheral events as first-class behavior.
findings.evidence: Timing/Bus/JIT and push/event references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/MANIFEST.md:31`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:66`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:169`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:282`
findings.impact: A guest can generate events faster than rendering, audio, networking, or tracing consumers can process them, causing memory growth or timing distortion.
findings.change: Use bounded queues, coalescing rules for replaceable state, explicit drop counters, and deterministic backpressure for lossless channels.
findings.acceptance: Stress tests sustain maximum event rates with bounded memory and documented loss/latency behavior.

findings.title: Prove host-mode parity as a product invariant
findings.strength: The same project supports interactive use and automated proof, which is strategically valuable.
findings.evidence: Live canvas, headless, and replay references span `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:243`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:53`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:187`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/speed-plan.md:132`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/examples/waveshare-cam/README.md:6`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/examples/waveshare-cam/run-autopling.sh:3`
findings.impact: Separate implementations can drift in imports, validation, timing, defaults, and error handling, creating “passes headless, fails live” or the reverse.

findings.title: Correct the roadmap assumption that a Bus wrapper observes all memory traffic
findings.strength: The roadmap wisely seeks a narrow timing/observation seam instead of scattering instrumentation.
findings.evidence: ESP32Sim exposes fast-memory/JIT paths at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:200`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:72`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:143`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:187`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/bus.rs:59`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/esp32s3/src/bus.rs:622`
findings.impact: The native JIT probes the TLB and performs host loads/stores directly on fast paths. Those operations bypass ordinary `Bus` read/write methods, so a wrapper around the trait cannot see all accesses or enforce complete timing/accounting.

findings.acceptance: A conformance program exercises RAM, flash, MMIO, faults, self-modifying code, and cross-page accesses; interpreter, JIT-fast, and JIT-hooked modes produce identical observations and timing.

findings.title: Put ESP32Sim behind a Puck-owned stable adapter
findings.strength: ESP32Sim already separates CPU, SoC, board, CLI, and web concerns—excellent raw material for an adapter.
findings.evidence: CPU/SoC/board and Bus-related structure is visible around `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/MANIFEST.md:31`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:66`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:169`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:282`

findings.change: Create a small adapter contract: create/reset, load image, run-to-deadline, inject event, drain typed events, bounded memory inspection, capabilities, snapshot metadata, and shutdown. No Puck code outside the adapter imports upstream internals.

findings.title: Specify the scheduler and virtual-time contract before peripheral work
findings.strength: Both projects already care about exact output timing and deterministic regression.
findings.evidence: Timing/roadmap references appear in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:1`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:11`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:1`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:61` and fast-path timing in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/MANIFEST.md:31`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:66`
findings.impact: Without a written definition of cycle ownership, deadlines, device flushes, host pacing, and simultaneous events, two correct-looking implementations can diverge at interrupts, DMA completion, touch polling, or audio boundaries.
findings.change: Write an ADR defining monotonic virtual cycles, event priority/tie-breaks, CPU/device advancement, deadline semantics, host pacing separation, and what “exact” means for each test tier.
findings.acceptance: Table-driven scheduler tests cover same-cycle IRQs, DMA completion, timer compare, reset, sleep, and host input at boundaries.

findings.title: Treat the interpreter as the semantic oracle and JIT as an optional optimization
findings.strength: ESP32Sim’s `--no-jit` path and bit-identical comparisons are a particularly valuable design choice.
findings.evidence: JIT and interpreter references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:200`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:72`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:143`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:187`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/bus.rs:59`
findings.impact: A native-code backend increases unsafe-code, executable-memory, invalidation, and architecture-specific risk. It must not become the only path capable of running tests or observing behavior.
findings.change: Keep interpreter support mandatory in all environments; gate JIT by capability and trust level; run differential programs across both on every relevant change.
findings.acceptance: Release CI includes interpreter/JIT differential suites; untrusted/headless proof mode can disable JIT without losing functionality.

findings.title: Design snapshot and reset semantics before exposing save/restore
findings.strength: The model already distinguishes chip, board, and runtime state, which is a good basis for snapshots.
findings.evidence: Reset/replay concepts appear in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:38`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:53`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:149`
findings.impact: A partial snapshot that omits pending DMA, device deadlines, TLB/JIT versions, network state, RNG, or host queues can resume into impossible state and invalidate regressions.
findings.change: Version a complete deterministic snapshot schema or explicitly defer snapshots. Separate immutable board wiring from resettable chip state and non-serializable live host resources.
findings.acceptance: Save/restore at randomized cycle boundaries yields the same final event hash as uninterrupted execution, or the capability is absent rather than partial.

findings.title: Make dual-core and interrupt ordering observable and testable
findings.strength: ESP32Sim’s deterministic scheduling is more suitable for regression than unconstrained host threading.
findings.evidence: CPU/interrupt timing concepts are present in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:3`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:4`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:9`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:10`
findings.impact: Small changes in core interleave, interrupt sampling, or device flush timing can alter FreeRTOS behavior while still producing plausible output.
findings.change: Document core quantum and tie-break order; expose deterministic trace events for core step, IRQ assert/accept, and device deadline; create race-sensitive litmus firmware.
findings.acceptance: Litmus tests and real-hardware traces pin ordering; changing the policy requires an ADR and fixture review.

findings.title: Assign one authoritative owner for each address range and peripheral event
findings.strength: The CPU/SoC/board layering makes ownership explicit enough to formalize.
findings.evidence: Bus/peripheral references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/MANIFEST.md:31`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:66`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:169`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:282`
findings.impact: Overlapping maps, mirrored ranges, “default zero” reads, and duplicated device ticks can hide unsupported behavior and make debugging nonlinear.
findings.change: Generate an address-map registry with range, access widths, reset values, owner, side effects, unsupported policy, and test status. Reject overlaps unless declared aliases.
findings.acceptance: A map audit test detects overlap/gaps; unknown accesses are traceable and can be configured to fault in strict mode.

findings.title: Keep board revision and wiring data declarative
findings.strength: The project already distinguishes board-level evidence from generic SoC work.
findings.evidence: Board revision references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/DEVELOPING.md:155`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/DEVELOPING.md:158`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/tools/classify-tearing.py:13`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/tools/classify-tearing.py:49`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/esp32/dependencies.lock:12`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/esp32/dependencies.lock:91`
findings.impact: Conditionals spread across display, touch, GPIO, and scripts make revision support difficult to test and easy to mix accidentally.
findings.change: Define a versioned board manifest for flash/PSRAM, pins, buses, display/touch controllers, geometry, polarity, clock limits, and fixtures; construct models from it.
findings.acceptance: Both revisions parse through one schema; invalid or incomplete wiring fails before boot; generated documentation matches the manifest.

findings.title: Publish a native/browser capability matrix
findings.strength: ESP32Sim’s browser build is a major strategic advantage.
findings.evidence: WebAssembly and network/JIT code paths appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:224`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:225`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/server.ts:183`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/server.ts:185`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/speed-plan.md:117`
findings.impact: Native and browser builds differ materially: JIT, sockets/NAT, filesystem, performance, threads, and possibly timers. A single “supported” label can mislead users and tests.
findings.change: Expose machine-readable capabilities and document support levels by backend. Tests should skip only with an explicit unsupported capability—not silently due to missing files.
findings.acceptance: The UI and CLI report capabilities; the matrix is generated from code and checked against conformance results.

findings.title: Gate performance work on semantic and security invariants
findings.strength: Upstream performance work is measured and often compared against bit-identical outputs, which is excellent practice.
findings.evidence: Fast memory/JIT references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:200`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:72`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:143`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:187`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/bus.rs:59`
findings.impact: Optimization can bypass validation, instrumentation, version checks, or exact timing—as the Bus observation gap demonstrates.
findings.change: Require a checklist for every fast path: semantic oracle comparison, boundary hooks, quota accounting, invalidation, fault behavior, deterministic output, and hostile-input tests.
findings.acceptance: No performance PR merges without before/after conformance hashes and security-boundary coverage; speed results are secondary acceptance evidence.

findings.title: Define the firmware and ESP-IDF compatibility promise
findings.strength: Booting unmodified firmware and real ROMs is a compelling product direction.
findings.evidence: `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:3`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:4`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:9`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:10`
findings.impact: “ESP32-S3 compatible” can mean booting one fixture, one IDF family, or broad silicon behavior. New IDF releases exercise new ROM calls, peripheral modes, and security paths.
findings.change: Publish tested IDF/Arduino versions, boot modes, chips, board revisions, and peripheral feature levels. Add representative firmware per supported band and label everything else experimental.
findings.acceptance: Each release carries a generated compatibility report with exact toolchain and firmware hashes.

findings.title: Create an explicit upstream API/ABI version
findings.strength: The source layout is modular enough to expose a deliberately small public surface.
findings.evidence: Workspace structure and adapter-relevant symbols appear around `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:3`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:4`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:9`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:10`
findings.impact: Without versioned behavior, Puck cannot tell whether an upstream update changed event semantics, timing, or only implementation.
findings.change: Version the adapter protocol and event schema independently of package version; require capability negotiation and reject incompatible major versions.
findings.acceptance: Old fixture manifests either continue to run under a compatibility layer or fail with a clear version error.

findings.title: Security-review bespoke JIT, crypto, packet, and image/audio parsing surfaces
findings.strength: A low external dependency count reduces third-party supply-chain exposure.
findings.evidence: Unsafe/JIT and network patterns appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:98`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:104`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:105`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:106`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:107`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:112` and `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:139`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:156`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:31`
findings.impact: Low dependencies shift responsibility into project code. Raw-pointer JIT helpers, executable memory, packet parsers, decompression/image code, and custom crypto arithmetic are high-consequence host attack surfaces when firmware is untrusted.
findings.change: Inventory every `unsafe` block and parser, state safety invariants, isolate JIT, fuzz byte-oriented inputs, run sanitizers/Miri where applicable, and prefer audited libraries for host-security functions.
findings.acceptance: Unsafe-code review has owners; fuzz targets run continuously; sanitizer builds are clean; untrusted mode can disable high-risk optional features.

findings.title: Separate emulated correctness from host-service convenience
findings.strength: ESP32Sim’s virtual AP/NAT and host UI make real applications demonstrable.
findings.evidence: Network and web service code appears at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:139`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:156`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:31`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/README.md:12`
findings.impact: Host clock, DNS, NAT, WebSockets, and filesystem output are conveniences, not silicon. Mixing them into machine semantics complicates determinism and widens trusted code.
findings.change: Keep host services behind interfaces with deterministic transcript implementations for tests and policy-enforced live implementations for demos.
findings.acceptance: The same firmware can run with `none`, deterministic transcript, and live service providers; machine-state hashes exclude non-semantic host timing.

findings.title: Set honest performance expectations per host architecture
findings.strength: Upstream publishes measured workloads instead of one synthetic headline number.
findings.evidence: JIT-specific code and browser paths appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:200`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:72`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:143`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:187`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/bus.rs:59`
findings.impact: The native JIT is architecture-specific; x86 and WebAssembly can use different execution engines and therefore different throughput and risk profiles.
findings.change: Benchmark a small canonical suite on supported macOS/Linux/Windows architectures and browser engines; publish median and worst-case real-time factors with JIT status.
findings.acceptance: Release notes contain reproducible benchmark manifests and no cross-host extrapolation.

findings.title: Use a small, reviewable patch stack for the fork
findings.strength: The upstream project is active enough that selective synchronization may be valuable.
findings.evidence: Local and public commit metadata are recorded in the review evidence; the public head may continue moving quickly.
findings.impact: A long-lived fork with mixed product features and upstream fixes becomes difficult to audit, license, or rebase.
findings.change: Keep Puck-specific behavior in adapter/board crates where possible; maintain upstream commits as clean cherry-picks and product patches as separately labeled commits.
findings.acceptance: An automated range-diff summarizes every upstream sync and the conformance suite runs before and after it.

findings.title: Expand required CI from pack/registry checks to the actual product proof matrix
findings.strength: The existing required workflow establishes a useful starting gate for artifact integrity.
findings.evidence: Inspected workflow commands: `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/.github/workflows/pages.yml:25` → `tools/wasm-build.sh`; `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/.github/workflows/pages.yml:27` → `|`; `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/.github/workflows/pages.yml:36` → `|`; `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/.github/workflows/verify-bundles.yml:39` → `|`; `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/.github/workflows/verify-bundles.yml:54` → `bun run tools/ci-verify-registry.ts`; `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/.github/workflows/verify-bundles.yml:57` → `bun run pack:esp32:gate`. The reviewed required slice does not enforce the full typecheck, hostile-host, regression, browser, and ESP32Sim Rust matrix described by the project.
findings.impact: Safeguards that are not required checks can regress while PRs remain green; prose and local scripts are not enforcement.
findings.change: Create required jobs for formatting/lint, strict typecheck, unit tests, hostile modules, headless regressions, browser smoke/parity, pack/registry validation, Rust fmt/test/clippy, and decoder conformance with real corpora.
findings.acceptance: Branch rules require every job; a deliberately broken validator, fixture, type, browser path, and Rust decoder each causes the expected required job to fail.

findings.title: Make decoder conformance fail closed when corpora are absent
findings.strength: Differential decoding against vendor/objdump output is exactly the right high-value oracle.
findings.evidence: External decoder corpus variables and skip paths appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/cli.md:61`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/testing-plan.md:39`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/tests/objdump_diff.rs:3`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/tests/objdump_diff.rs:25`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/esp32c3.md:126`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/riscv-rv32/tests/objdump_diff.rs:3`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/riscv-rv32/tests/objdump_diff.rs:26`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/riscv-rv32/tests/objdump_diff.rs:27`
findings.impact: A test that returns success when files are missing converts the headline conformance claim into an optional local check. CI can report green without running it.

findings.acceptance: Required logs report nonzero Xtensa and RISC-V case counts and exact corpus digests; removing the artifact makes the job fail, not skip.

findings.title: Grow the mandatory Rust semantic test base beyond the current smoke level
findings.strength: The existing tests cover important decoder and cryptographic examples, and the codebase remains small enough to improve quickly.

findings.impact: A full CPU/SoC emulator can pass a small suite while instruction corner cases, exceptions, memory faults, MMU invalidation, peripheral timing, and reset behavior remain untested.
findings.change: Add table/property tests for every instruction family and exception; state-machine tests for peripherals; scheduler litmus tests; and mandatory firmware boot fixtures.
findings.acceptance: Coverage reports meaningful semantic categories, not only lines; every modeled peripheral and instruction family has positive, boundary, and fault tests.

findings.title: Add fuzzing, property testing, sanitizers, and unsafe-code checks
findings.strength: The deterministic cores and parsers are excellent candidates for automated generative testing.
findings.evidence: Unsafe, panic, and parser-adjacent patterns appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0005-rca-core1-dies-on-first-button.md:80`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:98`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:104`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:105`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:106`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:107`
findings.impact: Handwritten decoders, JIT encoders, memory maps, WASI imports, packets, manifests, and image/audio paths have combinatorial input spaces that examples will not cover.
findings.change: Add cargo-fuzz/libFuzzer targets, property tests, Address/UndefinedBehavior sanitizers for native helpers, Miri for suitable Rust modules, and JS/Wasm hostile corpus mutation.
findings.acceptance: Nightly jobs run bounded fuzz campaigns, preserve minimized reproducers, and show zero sanitizer/Miri findings on the supported subset.

findings.title: Make branch protection and review rules part of the documented system
findings.strength: The project already has governance-oriented documentation.
findings.evidence: Workflow files exist at puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/.github/workflows/pages.yml, puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/.github/workflows/verify-bundles.yml, but branch-rule state is not contained in a source archive.
findings.impact: Required checks, signed commits, review counts, and force-push policy can silently differ from the documented development process.
findings.change: Store rules as code where possible, document required repository settings, and run a periodic GitHub API audit that compares actual settings to policy.
findings.acceptance: An audit job reports protected default branch, required checks, restricted force pushes/deletion, and review requirements.

findings.title: Promote browser smoke and parity tests to required status
findings.strength: A browser-native emulator is a core differentiator, not a secondary demo.
findings.evidence: Browser/WebAssembly paths appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:224`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/AGENTS.md:225`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/server.ts:183`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/server.ts:185`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/speed-plan.md:117`
findings.impact: Typechecks and headless tests will not catch Worker startup, CSP, cache, structured-clone, audio/canvas, memory-growth, and lifecycle failures.
findings.change: Run Playwright/WebDriver against a production build in at least Chromium and one second engine; exercise load, run, stop, reset, hostile module, reload/cache, and parity hashes.
findings.acceptance: Browser jobs are required, deterministic, capture console errors, and fail on uncaught rejection, CSP violation, resource leak, or result mismatch.

findings.title: Require semantic review for golden updates
findings.strength: Bit-identical display/audio/trace fixtures are powerful change detectors.
findings.evidence: Regression/golden behavior is referenced in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:38`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:53`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:149`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:157`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:187`
findings.impact: Goldens answer “did it change,” not “is it correct.” A bug can be accepted by regenerating all outputs.
findings.change: Pair each golden with semantic assertions: dimensions, frame count, selected pixels/regions, event sequence, audio duration/rate/energy, serial milestones, and no unexpected warnings. Require a diff summary on update.
findings.acceptance: A fixture update cannot merge without a machine-generated semantic diff and reviewer acknowledgement of each changed invariant.

findings.title: Record complete fixture provenance and environment
findings.strength: Exact fixture hashes are already a strong start.
findings.evidence: Integrity references appear in `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:87`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:93`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:126`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:115`
findings.impact: A hash alone does not explain which firmware, board config, seed, clock, emulator commit, toolchain, or event script produced it.
findings.change: Generate a sidecar manifest for each run with all source/artifact hashes, backend capabilities, flags, virtual duration, seed, input script, host architecture, and result hashes.
findings.acceptance: A fixture is rejected if any required provenance field is missing; one command reproduces it from approved inputs.

findings.title: Automate a small hardware-in-the-loop oracle
findings.strength: The project has real-silicon receipts, which are more valuable than speculative datasheet interpretation.
findings.evidence: Board/calibration references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:3`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:51`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:58`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:128`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:40`
findings.impact: Manual hardware captures are hard to rerun and can drift from the firmware/config used by the emulator.
findings.change: Create a controlled HIL job or scheduled lab run that flashes exact firmware, captures serial/JTAG/display/touch traces, normalizes nondeterministic fields, and publishes signed artifacts.
findings.acceptance: At least one boot/timer/GPIO/display/touch specimen per supported board revision is periodically compared with emulator output.

findings.title: Test validators by mutation, not only handpicked bad cases
findings.strength: Hostile-module awareness is already present in the project’s design.
findings.evidence: Hostile/malformed references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/testing-plan.md:364`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/decisions/0005-external-ports-are-reproduced.md:77`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/decisions/0005-external-ports-are-reproduced.md:79`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/findings-first-adversarial-pass.md:1`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/findings-first-adversarial-pass.md:4`
findings.impact: Handwritten invalid fixtures often miss arithmetic combinations, stale-memory timing, duplicate messages, and near-limit cases.
findings.change: Generate mutations of valid modules/manifests/events: pointers, lengths, dimensions, counts, alignment, memory growth, output ordering, and truncation. Minimize and retain failures.
findings.acceptance: Mutation score is tracked; each validator branch is killed by at least one mutation across every host mode.

findings.title: Add fault-injection campaigns for peripheral and host failures
findings.strength: The architecture has explicit boundaries where faults can be injected cleanly.
findings.evidence: Peripheral, replay, and network references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/MANIFEST.md:31`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:66`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:169`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:282`
findings.impact: Real systems see short reads, DMA faults, malformed packets, missing devices, reset mid-transfer, disk-full, worker termination, and browser context loss.
findings.change: Introduce deterministic fault schedules at bus, device, filesystem, network, Worker, and artifact-commit boundaries; assert safe recovery or clear terminal failure.
findings.acceptance: Every boundary has at least one injected failure test and no fault can produce a false pass or corrupt known-good fixtures.

findings.title: Measure boundary coverage, not only source-line coverage
findings.strength: The project’s architecture documents provide a natural inventory of boundaries.
findings.evidence: `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:1`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:11`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:1`
findings.impact: High line coverage can coexist with untested modes, error paths, capabilities, instruction families, and peripheral states.
findings.change: Maintain a coverage matrix for host modes × guest behaviors × backends × board revisions × trust faults. Use code coverage as supporting evidence, not the sole metric.
findings.acceptance: Release reports show no empty cells for required boundaries and explain experimental cells explicitly.

findings.title: Enforce timeouts, leak checks, and clean shutdown in tests
findings.strength: Deterministic virtual-time tests can be both strict and fast.
findings.evidence: Headless and Worker/runtime references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:38`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:53`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:149`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:157`
findings.impact: A test can pass while leaving Workers, sockets, timers, temp files, executable mappings, or queued messages alive, creating order-dependent CI failures.
findings.change: Wrap each integration test with wall timeout, resource baseline/delta checks, temp-dir isolation, explicit shutdown, and post-test open-handle detection.
findings.acceptance: Tests pass in randomized order and repeated loops with stable memory, descriptor, process, and temporary-file counts.

findings.title: Pin the complete build toolchain, not only dependencies
findings.strength: Lockfiles and exact artifacts support reproducibility.
findings.evidence: Package manager metadata: `None`; engines: `None`. Tool-version probe results are in the companion test log.
findings.impact: Bun/Node/Rust/LLVM/browser/ESP-IDF changes can alter emitted Wasm, decoding, floating behavior, fixtures, or CI scripts without a source change.
findings.change: Pin versions through toolchain files/container digests; print them in every result manifest; provide a hermetic bootstrap path.
findings.acceptance: Two clean machines build byte-identical or explicitly normalized artifacts from the same source and toolchain image.

findings.title: Generate attestations and an SBOM for release artifacts
findings.strength: The project’s content hashes make attestation straightforward.
findings.evidence: Hashing/integrity evidence appears at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:87`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:93`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:126`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:115`
findings.impact: Users and future maintainers need to know which source, tools, dependencies, firmware, and upstream fork produced a browser bundle or native binary.
findings.change: Generate SPDX/CycloneDX SBOMs, provenance attestations, checksums, license notices, and signed release manifests in a protected release workflow.
findings.acceptance: A release verifier can validate artifact digest, source commit, builder identity, dependency graph, and license inventory offline.

findings.title: Check documentation links, claims, and generated matrices in CI
findings.strength: The documentation is unusually substantive and deserves to remain trustworthy.
findings.evidence: Documentation/roadmap references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:1`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:11`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:1`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:61`

findings.strength: ESP32Sim’s upstream history shows careful interleaved measurements and output comparisons—preserve that standard.
findings.evidence: Performance/JIT paths appear around `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:200`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:72`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:143`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/xtensa-lx7/src/block.rs:187`

findings.title: Treat SH8601/FT3168 support as unvalidated inherited evidence
findings.strength: Retaining the earlier revision’s notes is useful research, not wasted work.

findings.title: Capture controller transactions before coding detailed display/touch models
findings.strength: TinyDraw and calibration assets provide excellent expected visuals.
findings.evidence: Display/touch/controller references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:3`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:51`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:58`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:128`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:40`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:368`

findings.change: Capture reset/power sequence, SPI/QSPI writes, DMA descriptors, frame windows, touch I2C transactions/interrupts, and orientation transforms from real hardware.

findings.title: Preserve banded DMA, but specify memory and backpressure invariants
findings.strength: The banded design is a strong, practical response to display memory pressure.
findings.evidence: Framebuffer/push and board references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:65`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:74`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:75`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:78`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:273`
findings.impact: Without explicit maximum band size, stride/alignment, ownership, queue depth, and completion semantics, the optimization can introduce overruns or visual tearing.
findings.change: Document buffer ownership and lifecycle, prevalidate all band geometry, cap in-flight bands, and test odd widths, last partial band, orientation, and slow-consumer behavior.
findings.acceptance: Memory use stays below a fixed ceiling; randomized band layouts reproduce the full-frame reference exactly and never write outside buffers.

findings.title: Model reset, flash, PSRAM, and boot conditions before rich peripherals
findings.strength: ESP32Sim’s real-ROM/full-boot capability is the correct foundation for realistic firmware.
findings.evidence: Boot/board/SoC references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:3`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:4`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:9`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:10`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:17`
findings.impact: Peripheral demos can appear healthy while reset cause, straps, flash size/mode, partition offsets, PSRAM mapping, or retained state are wrong.
findings.change: Create a board boot contract and conformance fixture for power-on, software reset, watchdog reset, flash/PSRAM geometry, straps, and partition loading.
findings.acceptance: Boot logs and selected register/memory checkpoints match real hardware for each supported reset mode.

findings.title: Stage Wi-Fi/BLE after deterministic local board behavior
findings.strength: ESP32Sim demonstrates impressive unmodified Wi-Fi progress, so this can be a later differentiator.
findings.evidence: Network/Wi-Fi code appears at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:139`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:156`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/roadmap.md:31`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/README.md:12`
findings.impact: Radio blobs, virtual AP behavior, crypto accelerators, NAT, host DNS/time, and nondeterminism greatly widen the model and security surface.

findings.title: Make hardware evidence a release artifact, not tribal knowledge
findings.strength: The current real-silicon receipts are a major strength.
findings.evidence: Calibration/board references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:3`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:51`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:58`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/docs/roadmap.md:128`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:40`
findings.impact: Screenshots or notes without exact firmware and capture metadata are difficult for future agents to reproduce or challenge.
findings.change: Store normalized traces, photos/screenshots, logic captures, firmware hashes, board serial/revision, probe scripts, and interpretation notes under a signed evidence manifest.
findings.acceptance: Every hardware-backed claim in the support matrix links to a reproducible evidence bundle.

findings.title: Detect or require board revision explicitly
findings.strength: Separate manifests make multiple revisions manageable.
findings.evidence: Revision/controller evidence appears at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/DEVELOPING.md:155`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/DEVELOPING.md:158`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/tools/classify-tearing.py:13`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/tools/classify-tearing.py:49`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/esp32/dependencies.lock:12`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/esp32/dependencies.lock:91`
findings.impact: Silently assuming a controller can send incompatible initialization commands or misinterpret touch coordinates.
findings.change: Use a trusted build/manifest selection or safe read-only probe where hardware permits; display the selected revision and reject ambiguous configurations.
findings.acceptance: Wrong-revision fixtures fail early with a clear diagnostic, never with a blank screen or partially working touch.

findings.title: Lock down pixel format, endian, stride, clipping, and orientation with property tests
findings.strength: TinyDraw calibration material is well suited to precise visual conformance.
findings.evidence: Framebuffer and controller references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/DEVELOPING.md:155`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/DEVELOPING.md:158`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/tools/classify-tearing.py:13`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/tools/classify-tearing.py:49`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/tinydraw/esp32/dependencies.lock:12`
findings.impact: Display bugs often hide in odd widths, byte order, negative clipping, rotated coordinates, alpha/premultiplication, and final partial rows.
findings.change: Define canonical internal pixel format and conversion boundaries. Add generated patterns and random rectangles across all orientations, strides, and edge coordinates.
findings.acceptance: Reference hashes and pixel probes match software rendering and captured hardware; out-of-range geometry is rejected before memory access.

findings.title: Keep unsupported controller behavior explicit rather than plausible
findings.strength: The roadmap’s candid unknowns are a strong habit to preserve.
findings.evidence: TODO/unimplemented references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:77`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/architecture.md:78`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0002-runtime-architecture.md:366`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/esp32-s3-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/README.md:8`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:253`
findings.impact: Returning zero, success, or a fabricated status for unknown commands can let firmware proceed into misleading state and make later debugging much harder.
findings.change: In strict mode, trace and fail on unsupported operations; in compatibility mode, log a stable warning with call count and source. Never silently claim support.
findings.acceptance: Support reports list every exercised unsupported operation; a release target has none in its required fixtures.

findings.title: Remove panic/unchecked assumptions from untrusted-input paths
findings.strength: Rust and TypeScript make explicit error handling practical.
findings.evidence: Potential panic/unsafe sites appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/packs/rp2350-touch-amoled-18/docs/decisions/0005-rca-core1-dies-on-first-button.md:80`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:98`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:104`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:105`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:106`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:107`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:112`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/cli-c3/src/main.rs:115`
findings.impact: An `unwrap`, assertion, unchecked index, or panic reachable from firmware, packet, manifest, or file input turns a guest fault into a host-process denial of service.
findings.change: Classify call sites by trust, replace reachable panics with typed errors, add bounds checks before indexing, and reserve assertions for internal invariants proven by validated types.
findings.acceptance: A panic hook test runs hostile corpora and observes zero host panics; remaining panics are documented unreachable invariants with tests.

findings.title: Reduce duplicated host logic by extracting validated domain types
findings.strength: The live validator already contains the seeds of reusable domain types.
findings.evidence: Validation/framebuffer/headless references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/abiGuard.ts:95`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/abiGuard.ts:124`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/panel.ts:20`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/panel.ts:49`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/src/panel.ts:55`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/site/dist/emu/main.js:28`
findings.impact: Passing primitive tuples and raw pointers between layers invites repeated checks, inconsistent units, and accidental bypass.
findings.change: Introduce constructors for validated guest ranges, framebuffer descriptors, pixel bands, log chunks, event timestamps, and artifact IDs; make invalid states unrepresentable.
findings.acceptance: Raw guest numeric fields are confined to the ABI module; downstream code accepts only validated types.

findings.title: Put explicit size and numeric conversion helpers in one module
findings.strength: Central helpers can make the existing hardening concise rather than repetitive.
findings.evidence: Numeric pointer/length and MAX references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/speed-plan.md:70`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/docs/decisions.md:182`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/esp32c3/src/machine.rs:42`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/esp32c3/src/machine.rs:56`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/esp32c3/src/machine.rs:183`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/esp32sim/esp32c3/src/machine.rs:187`
findings.impact: JavaScript number coercion, signed/unsigned conversion, multiplication overflow, and Rust `usize` conversion differ across 32/64-bit and Wasm/native environments.
findings.change: Use checked helpers for guest `u32/u64`, add/multiply/range, `usize` conversion, dimensions, and byte counts. Reject NaN, infinities, fractional values, negatives, and wraparound.
findings.acceptance: Cross-language boundary vectors produce the same accept/reject decision and error code.

findings.title: Separate debug instrumentation from correctness semantics
findings.strength: Tracing and visualization are valuable for reverse engineering and agent productivity.
findings.evidence: Trace/debug and Bus/JIT references appear at `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/MANIFEST.md:31`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:30`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:66`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:169`, `puck-esp32s3-export-2026-08-31/puck/README.md:282`
findings.impact: Instrumentation that changes scheduling, memory path, allocations, or device flush cadence can make the observed bug disappear or produce a different machine.
findings.change: Define zero-semantic-effect event taps; test tracing on/off equivalence; document any mode that intentionally disables optimization and compare it with the oracle.
findings.acceptance: The same deterministic workload has identical semantic hashes with logging/tracing enabled and disabled, excluding the trace artifact itself.

findings.title: Bound caches and make invalidation observable
findings.strength: ESP32Sim’s TLB/block/JIT caches are an effective performance strategy.

not_to_do: Do not start a deep merge or product fork of ESP32Sim until its repository-level license and the bundled asset rights are explicit in writing.
Do not assume that wrapping ESP32Sim’s `Bus` trait observes every memory access; the JIT fast path bypasses it.
Do not maintain separate validation logic for live canvas, headless replay, regression, and verification hosts.
Do not dereference guest pointers, iovecs, dimensions, counts, or strings before checked range and quota validation.
Do not trust cached typed-array views across guest calls that may grow WebAssembly memory.
Do not run untrusted firmware in the same long-lived process that adjudicates or publishes test results.
Do not enable native NAT or unrestricted host networking by default; never allow untrusted firmware implicit access to localhost, private networks, or metadata services.
Do not expose a control WebSocket beyond loopback without explicit authentication, Origin validation, TLS, and size/rate limits.
Do not let a required conformance test silently pass because its external corpus or firmware file is missing.
Do not treat a golden image, WAV, trace, or serial transcript as proof of correctness by itself.
Do not regenerate goldens in the same opaque step that changes behavior; require a semantic diff and provenance update.
Do not target CO5300/CST820 and SH8601/FT3168 simultaneously; finish the evidence-backed V2 vertical slice first.
Do not advertise original-revision support until that exact board has independent hardware traces and conformance results.
Do not expose ESP32Sim internal machine, bus, JIT, or peripheral types throughout Puck; keep a Puck-owned adapter boundary.
Do not make JIT availability a correctness requirement or enable it first in untrusted proof modes.
Do not optimize past validators, quota accounting, memory hooks, cache invalidation, or exact timing checks.
Do not silently return plausible zeros or success for unsupported registers, commands, or peripheral states in strict mode.
Do not allow guest or manifest names to become filesystem paths, cache keys, DOM HTML, or shell arguments without canonicalization.
Do not run arbitrary install/build scripts in trusted developer or release environments without isolation and a reviewed allowlist.
Do not pin GitHub Actions, toolchains, ROMs, or archives only by mutable tag/URL; verify immutable commits and digests.
Do not publish firmware, ROMs, SDK-derived binaries, media, or calibration assets until their redistribution status is recorded.
Do not let agents update architecture, ABI, timing, fixtures, and upstream pins in one unreviewable change; split decisions and preserve rollback points.
Do not interpret the upstream project’s rapid progress as a stable maintenance or compatibility guarantee; own the fork and its tests.
Do not claim cross-platform performance from Apple Silicon JIT measurements; report backend, host, workload, and semantic mode.
Do not call the project release-ready until the security boundary, required CI matrix, provenance, and hardware acceptance gates are all enforced.
